subject: basic-computing
title: Operating System
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Start button, Task Bar, Computer icon and Network icon are most used ______ elements.
questions.answer: Desktop.

questions.q: Windows provides a quick and easy way to ______ new software and hardware programs.
questions.answer: Install.

questions.q: Name the feature of Windows which helps in file management.
questions.answer: Windows Explorer (or Computer).

questions.q: By using ______ tools you can customize the way Windows looks and works.
questions.answer: Control Panel.

questions.q: Where do deleted files from the hard disk go first?
questions.answer: Into the Recycle Bin.

questions.q: What is the shortcut key to copy a selected file?
questions.answer: Ctrl + C.

questions.q: Where does the task bar appear by default on the screen?
questions.answer: At the bottom of the screen.

questions.q: Which key is pressed with the mouse to select non-consecutive files?
questions.answer: The Ctrl key.

questions.q: Which key must be held to delete a file permanently?
questions.answer: The Shift key (Shift + Delete).

questions.q: What does the Computer icon show?
questions.answer: The disk drives (hard disk, CD/DVD, pen drive) and hardware connected to the computer.

questions.q: Name the menu option that shows all installed programs.
questions.answer: All Programs in the Start menu.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Ravi has created a file ABC and later wants to change its name to PROJECT_ABC. Write the steps.
questions.answer: Step 1: Open Windows Explorer/Documents and click the file ABC. Step 2: Under File choose Rename (or right-click, Rename). Step 3: Type PROJECT_ABC and press Enter.

questions.q: Amit has saved a file with the name C1 but later wants it renamed as chart 1. Write the steps.
questions.answer: Step 1: Select the file C1. Step 2: Right-click and choose Rename (or File, Rename). Step 3: Type chart 1 and press Enter.

questions.q: Reeta wants to copy a file ABC to a folder XYZ. Write the steps.
questions.answer: Step 1: Select the file ABC. Step 2: Click Edit, Copy (Ctrl+C). Step 3: Open the folder XYZ. Step 4: Click Edit, Paste (Ctrl+V).

questions.q: Shyam has created a file QRT1 in a folder SALES. Later he wants to view its details. Write the steps.
questions.answer: Step 1: Open the folder SALES through Start, Documents. Step 2: Click the View menu. Step 3: Click Details; name, type, size and date of QRT1 are displayed.

questions.q: Define the following: (i) Task Bar (ii) File management in Windows.
questions.answer: (i) Task bar: the bar at the bottom of the screen showing the Start button and an icon for every open program or window. (ii) File management: creating, copying, moving, renaming, deleting and searching files and folders using Windows Explorer or Computer.

questions.q: Write the steps to create a new folder.
questions.answer: Step 1: Open Windows Explorer. Step 2: Click File, New, Folder. Step 3: Type the folder name over 'New Folder' and press Enter. (Or right-click on blank space, New, Folder.)

questions.q: Write the steps to delete a file and to restore it.
questions.answer: Delete: select the file, File, Delete (or right-click, Delete). Restore: double-click the Recycle Bin, right-click the file and choose Restore.

questions.q: Write the steps to uninstall a software.
questions.answer: Step 1: Click Start, Control Panel. Step 2: Choose Programs and Features. Step 3: Select the software. Step 4: Right-click and choose Uninstall.

questions.q: Write the steps to search for a file or folder.
questions.answer: Click Start, type the full or part name of the file or folder in the search box, and the results are listed.

questions.q: Write the steps to start a program such as Calculator.
questions.answer: Click Start, All Programs, Accessories, then click Calculator.

questions.q: How can one get help in Windows?
questions.answer: Click Start and choose Help and Support, then type the keywords on which help is needed.

questions.q: Differentiate between copying and moving a file.
questions.answer: Copying makes a duplicate and leaves the original in place; moving removes the file from the old place and puts it in the new location (drag with Shift or use Cut and Paste).

sections.title: Answer the questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the options in the Start menu.
questions.answer: All Programs lists installed programs; Documents, Pictures and Music open those folders; Computer shows drives; Control Panel changes settings; Devices and Printers lists hardware; Help and Support gives help; the search box finds files; Switch User, Log Off, Lock, Restart and Sleep manage the session.

questions.q: Describe how to copy and move a file using Windows Explorer.
questions.answer: Open Windows Explorer, select the file. To copy: Edit, Copy, open the target, Edit, Paste. To move: drag it to the destination (Shift while dragging between disks) or use Cut and Paste. Ctrl selects non-consecutive and Shift consecutive files.

questions.q: Explain how to install and uninstall a software.
questions.answer: Install: locate the setup (.exe) on CD/DVD/USB or after download, double-click it and follow the wizard; use it from All Programs. Uninstall: Start, Control Panel, Programs and Features, select the software, right-click, Uninstall.

questions.q: Describe file management in Windows and the role of the Recycle Bin.
questions.answer: Windows Explorer and Computer show the hierarchy of drives, folders and files and let you copy, move, rename, delete and search. Deleted hard-disk files go to the Recycle Bin and can be restored until it is emptied; removable-media files are deleted permanently.

questions.q: Explain the desktop elements of Windows.
questions.answer: Start button opens programs, search and shut down; the task bar shows open programs; the Computer icon shows drives and hardware; the Network icon shows connections; the Recycle Bin holds deleted files.
